([[chairman]] and [[Managing director|MD]])|Nitish Mittersain
([[CEO]] and joint MD){{cite web |title=About |publisher=Nazara Technologies |url=https://www.nazara.com/about|access-date=26 May 2024 }}}} | ISIN = INE418L01021 | revenue = {{up}} {{INRconvert|1138|c}} (FY24) | net_income = {{up}} {{INRconvert|89|c}} (FY24) | subsidiaries = {{plainlist| * [[WildWorks]] * Nextwave Multimedia * [[Kiddopia]] * [[Sportskeeda]] * Nodwin Gaming * Fusebox Games * [[Curve Games]]}} | website = {{URL|https://www.nazara.com}} }} '''Nazara Technologies''' is an Indian [[video game development]] company that has business interests in [[mobile game]]s, [[esports]], and [[sports media]]. Founded in 1999, it is based in [[Mumbai]], India, and through the years acquired several companies turned into [[subsidiaries]], including [[WildWorks]], [[Curve Games]], and [[Sportskeeda]]. == History == Nazara Technologies was founded in Mumbai by Nitish Mittersain as an [[Online game|online gaming]] portal in 1999, a year prior to the [[dotcom bust]].{{cite news |last=Khan |first=Taslima|title=For Nazara's IPO run, a long-haul horse |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/people/for-nazaras-ipo-run-a-long-haul-horse/articleshow/62207750.cms |access-date=24 July 2023 |work=The Times of India |date=22 December 2017}} In 2002, it switched to providing mobile entertainment [[Value-added service|VAS]] for telecom operators, including [[Wireless Application Protocol|WAP]] content downloads of [[comic strip]]s and mobile games.{{cite news |last=Talukdar |first=Tapash |title=Nazara: From gaming portal to mobile content |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/nazara-from-gaming-portal-to-mobile-content/articleshow/4019339.cms |access-date=26 May 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=23 January 2009}}{{cite news |last=Dash |first=Jayajit |title=Nazara plans new games for festive season |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/nazara-plans-new-games-for-festive-season-109092200036_1.html |access-date=24 May 2024 |date=22 September 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125213504/http://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/nazara-plans-new-games-for-festive-season-109092200036_1.html |archive-date=25 January 2021}}{{cite news |last=Chettri |first=Diwaskar |title=Updated: RCOM Launches Comics On Mobile For GSM |url=https://www.medianama.com/2010/01/223-reliance-communication-launches-comics-on-mobile-gsm-only/ |access-date=24 May 2024 |work=Medianama |date=24 January 2010}} Early [[likeness rights]] partnerships to deliver mobile content included those with [[Archie Comics]],{{cite news |title=Nazara, Archie Comics tie up |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/nazara-archie-comics-tie-up/articleshow/1037024.cms |access-date=26 May 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=1 March 2005}} [[Sachin Tendulkar]],{{cite news |last=Lohade |first=Nikhil |title=Catch Sachin on your cell |url=https://www.rediff.com/money/report/sachin/20050112.htm |access-date=26 May 2024 |work=Rediff |publisher=Business Standard |date=12 January 2005}} [[MS Dhoni]],{{cite news |title=Nazara to distribute mobile content of 'Dhoni's liking' |url=https://www.oneindia.com/2006/02/24/nazara-to-distribute-mobile-content-of-dhonis-liking-1140787781.html |access-date=26 May 2024 |work=Oneindia News|date=24 February 2006}} and [[Cartoon Network]].{{cite news |last=Chettri |first=Diwaskar |title=Comic VAS: Nazara Brings Cartoon Network To Mobiles |url=https://www.medianama.com/2009/12/223-comic-vas-nazara-brings-cartoon-network-to-mobiles/ |access-date=26 May 2024 |work=MediaNama |date=17 December 2009}} Nazara later expanded mobile games VAS into the [[Middle East]] and [[Africa]], also becoming the licensed [[digital distributor]] of [[EA Mobile]]'s games in these regions apart from [[South Asia]]n countries.{{cite news |title=Nazara Extends Games Distribution Partnership With EA To The Middle East |url=https://www.techcircle.in/2012/04/16/nazara-extends-games-distribution-partnership-with-ea-to-the-middle-east |access-date=24 May 2024 |work=Techcircle |date=16 April 2012 }}{{cite news |title=Nazara, EA sign distribution deal |url=https://www.itweb.co.za/article/nazara-ea-sign-distribution-deal/2JN1gP7OjX9vjL6m |work=ITWeb |date=17 March 2014|access-date=1 December 2025}} In 2015, Nazara obtained the license from [[Green Gold Animations]] to create mobile games based on ''[[Chhota Bheem]]'' animated television series.{{cite news |title=Nazara creates gaming franchisee with 'Chota Bheem' owner; to invest $7.6M |url=https://www.techcircle.in/2015/08/17/nazara-creates-gaming-franchisee-with-chota-bheem-owner-to-invest-7-6m |access-date=23 May 2024 |work=Techcircle |date=17 August 2015 }} In 2016, Nazara tied up with Indian comics company [[Amar Chitra Katha]] to develop mobile games on ''[[Tinkle]]'' characters like [[Shikari Shambu]].{{cite news |last=Ganguly |first=Shramana |title=Amar Chitra Katha ropes in Nazara Games to develop character- based mobile games |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/media/entertainment/amar-chitra-katha-ropes-in-nazara-games-to-develop-character-based-mobile-games/articleshow/50638932.cms |access-date=23 May 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=19 January 2016}} In 2018, Nazara acquired a majority stake in Nextwave Multimedia, a [[Chennai]]-based mobile game developer known for ''[[World Cricket Championship (mobile game)|World Cricket Championship]]'' titles.{{cite news |title=Gaming firm Nazara acquires majority stake in Chennai-based Nextwave |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/gaming-firm-nazara-acquires-majority-stake-in-chennaibased-nextwave/article10020449.ece |access-date=23 May 2024 |work=BusinessLine |date=8 January 2018 }} It also acquired 55% stake in esports firm Nodwin Gaming.{{cite news |last=Malik |first=Yuvraj |title=Nazara acquires majority stake in NODWIN Gaming |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/j6duyK7r4RlXNBfuydHUCK/Nazara-acquires-majority-stake-in-NODWIN-Gaming.html |access-date=23 May 2024 |work=mint |date=24 January 2018 }} Nazara was planning to go public in 2018 and had obtained approval from the market regulators, but halted the process.{{cite web |date=21 August 2019 |title=Gaming firm Nazara acquires Sportskeeda |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business-news/gaming-firm-nazara-acquires-sportskeeda/story-jXi2U3rOZsLfrKLRsgVH2L.html |access-date=6 June 2023 |website=[[Hindustan Times]]|last=Sriram|first=M.}} In 2019, Nazara Technologies purchased a 67% stake in Sportskeeda for ₹44 [[crore]]. It acquired a 51% stake in Paper Boat Apps, the developer and publisher of [[gamified early learning]] app Kiddopia, for {{INR}}83.5 crore in the same year.{{cite news |title=Nazara acquires majority stake in Paper Boat Apps |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/nazara-acquires-majority-stake-in-paper-boat-apps/articleshow/71629399.cms |access-date=23 May 2024 |work=The Times of India |date=17 October 2019}} In March 2021, Nazara was listed on the [[National Stock Exchange of India|NSE]] and [[Bombay Stock Exchange|BSE]] after its [[initial public offering]].{{cite news |title=Nazara Technologies shares list at 81% premium over issue price; Jhunjhunwala stake valued at Rs 656 crore |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/ipos/fpos/nazara-tech-shares-list-at-81-premium-over-issue-price-jhunjhunwala-stake-valued-at-rs-656-crore/articleshow/81753196.cms |access-date=24 July 2023 |work=The Economic Times }} Later the same year, it acquired the [[Hyderabad]]-based real-money gaming company OpenPlay for {{INR}}186 crore.{{cite web |date=August 28, 2021|last=Shah|first=Sneha|title=Nazara Technologies acquires OpenPlay for Rs 186 crore|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/startups/nazara-technologies-acquires-openplay-for-rs-186-crore/articleshow/85689708.cms|website=[[The Economic Times]]}} In 2022, Nazara acquired a 55% stake in Datawrkz, an advertising technology company based in [[Bangalore]], for {{INR}}124 crore.{{cite news |title=Nazara acquires majority stake in Datawrkz for Rs 124 crore |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/companies/nazara-acquires-majority-stake-in-datawrkz-for-rs-124-crore/articleshow/88968567.cms |access-date=23 May 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=18 January 2022}} Later that year, it bought out the US-based kids gaming company WildWorks for $10.4 million.{{cite news |last=Vardhan |first=Gyan |title=Nazara acquires US-based gaming company WildWorks |url=https://entrackr.com/2022/08/nazara-acquires-us-based-gaming-company-wildworks/ |access-date=23 May 2024 |work=Entrackr |date=30 August 2022}} In 2023, Nazara Technologies joined the All India Gaming Federation (AIGF) as a principal member.{{cite web |date=May 17, 2023|title=Nazara Technologies Joins All-India Gaming Federation (AIGF)|url=https://www.entrepreneur.com/en-in/news-and-trends/nazara-technologies-joins-all-india-gaming-federation-aigf/452311|last=Jose|first=Teena|website=Entrepreneur India}} In 2024, Nazara acquired [[Comic Con India]] for {{INR}}55 crore through its subsidiary Nodwin Gaming.{{cite news |title=Nazara Technologies to acquire Comic Con India via Nodwin Gaming |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/startups/nazara-technologies-to-acquire-comic-con-india-via-nodwin-gaming/articleshow/107098669.cms |access-date=26 May 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=24 January 2024}} On 8 Augus, 2024, it was announced that Nazara had acquired UK based Fusebox Games for $27.2 million. The company is known for making [[Love Island (2015 TV series)|Love Island]]-themed games since 2018.{{cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/nazara-buys-uks-fusebox-games-in-27-million-all-cash-deal/articleshow/112375587.cms?from=mdr |title=Nazara buys UK's Fusebox Games in $27-million all-cash deal|work=The Economic Times |access-date=8 August 2024}} In September 2024, Nazara Technologies acquired 47.7% stake in Moonshine Technology, the parent company of PokerBaazi for Rs 832 crore.{{cite web |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/startups/nazara-picks-up-47-stake-in-pokerbaazi-parent-moonshine-for-rs-832-crore/articleshow/113311951.cms?from=mdr |title=Nazara Tech acquires 47.7% stake in PokerBaazi parent in Rs 832 crore deal |work=The Economic Times |access-date=13 September 2024}} As of the 2024 fiscal year, the company reported an increased [[revenue]] and [[net income]], respectivaly at ₹1,138 crore (US$130 million) and ₹89 crore (US$11 million).{{cite web |title=Nazara Technologies' Q4 profit shrinks to Rs 0.18 cr, revenue declines to Rs 266.2 cr |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/technology/nazara-technologies-q4-profit-shrinks-to-rs-0-18-cr-revenue-declines-to-rs-266-2-cr-article-12731783.html |access-date=25 May 2024 |website=Moneycontrol |date=25 May 2024}} In January 2025, Nazara Technologies bought two mobile games ''[[King of Thieves (video game)|King of Thieves]]'' and ''[[CATS: Crash Arena Turbo Stars]]'' from [[Zeptolab]] for USD 7.7 million.{{cite web |last= |first= |date=21 January 2025 |title=Nazara Technologies Secures INR 495 Cr in Strategic Stake Sale, Eyes Global Expansion |url=https://www.entrepreneur.com/en-in/news-and-trends/nazara-technologies-secures-inr-495-cr-in-strategic-stake/485835 |access-date=23 February 2025 |website=Entrepreneur }} In May 2025, Nazara Technologies acquired Smaaash Entertainment, an arcade franchise from India that was rebranded as Zoreko a year prior, which provides on-venue activities like bowling, go-karting, and arcade gaming, as well as dining and drinking.{{cite news|title=Nazara's resolution plan to acquire Smaaash gets NCLT nod|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/nazaras-resolution-plan-to-acquire-smaaash-gets-nclt-nod/articleshow/120970416.cms|work=The Economic Times|date=7 May 2025|access-date=1 December 2025|issn=0013-0389}}{{cite web|title=Zerodha's Nikhil Kamath-backed Nazara Technologies' shares rise after NCLT clears Smaaash acquisition|url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/markets/zerodhas-nikhil-kamath-backed-nazara-technologies-shares-rise-after-nclt-clears-smaaash-acquisition/122870|website=Fortune India|date=8 May 2025|access-date=1 December 2025}} Also in May 2025, Nazara Technologies acquired British indie game publisher Curve Games, whose released titles include ''[[Human: Fall Flat]]''.{{cite web |last=Scullion |first=Chris |date=20 May 2025 |title=Human Fall Flat publisher Curve Games has been acquired by Nazara Technologies for £21.6m |url=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/human-fall-flat-publisher-curve-games-has-been-acquired-by-nazara-technologies-for-21-6m/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520141218/https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/human-fall-flat-publisher-curve-games-has-been-acquired-by-nazara-technologies-for-21-6m/ |archive-date=20 May 2025 |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=VGC }} == Subsidiaries == === Sportskeeda === [[File:Sportskeeda.svg|thumb|Sportskeeda logo]] Sportskeeda is a global sports and esports media [[subsidiary]] of Nazara Technologies headquartered in Bangalore, India. It features news, articles, and live coverage of sports such as [[cricket]], [[association football]], [[American football]], [[basketball]], [[mixed martial arts]], and [[professional wrestling]].{{cite web |last=SN |first=Vikas |date=16 November 2022 |title=Nazara's Sportskeeda appoints Ajay Pratap Singh as CEO; founder Porush Jain resigns |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/nazaras-sportskeeda-appoints-ajay-pratap-singh-as-ceo-founder-porush-jain-resigns-9549331.html |access-date=6 June 2023 |website=Moneycontrol }} In 2009, the company was founded by Porush Jain. After a few months, the company raised an undisclosed amount of funding from angel investors.{{cite web |last=Ghosh |first=Aparna |date=20 August 2014 |title=Online retail: Counting on sports lovers |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/PAvZ3lHzFtH6e97hAJ6hOK/Online-retail-Counting-on-sports-lovers.html |access-date=6 June 2023 |website=[[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]]}} In 2011, an early stage venture capital funding company, Seedfund, invested ₹2.8 crore.{{cite web |date=23 September 2012 |title=A social way of covering sports |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/A-social-way-of-covering-sports/article20505160.ece |access-date=6 June 2023 |website=[[Business Line]]|last=Ramakrishnan|first=N.}} In 2019, Nazara Technologies acquired a 67% stake in Sportskeeda for ₹44 crore, valuing Sportskeeda at ₹65 crore. In 2020, during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the company launched two video series: ''Freehit'' and ''SKlive'', featuring interviews with prominent sportspeople.{{cite web |last=Sabherwal |first=Simran |date=11 Sep 2020 |title=We want to be lean, yet grow fast: Porush Jain, Sportskeeda |url=https://www.exchange4media.com/marketing-news/we-want-to-be-lean-yet-grow-fast-porush-jain-sportskeeda-107512.html |access-date=6 June 2023 |website=Exchange4media }} In May 2022, Nazara set up its subsidiary Sportskeeda Inc. in [[Delaware]], US.{{cite web |date=27 May 2022 |title=Sportskeeda establishes an entity in the US; to invest USD 4 million into operations |url=https://theprint.in/ani-press-releases/sportskeeda-establishes-an-entity-in-the-us-to-invest-usd-4-million-into-operations/973644/ |access-date=18 November 2022 |website=ThePrint }} In November 2022, Porush Jain resigned as CEO and Ajay Pratap Singh was promoted to take his place. In 2023, Sportskeeda acquired a 73.27% stake in Pro Football Network LLC, a US-based sports analysis website that covers the [[NFL]] and [[college football]], for ₹16 crore (US$1.82 million).{{cite web |last=Gupta |first=Aryaman |date=22 March 2023 |title=Nazara arm Sportskeeda pays $1.8 mn for 73.27% stake in NFL-focused US firm |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/sportskeeda-acquires-majority-stake-in-nfl-focused-us-firm-for-1-8-mn-123032201122_1.html |access-date=6 June 2023 |website=[[Business Standard]]}} In 2024, Nazara Technologies further acquired 19.35 % for ₹145.5 crore in Absolute Sports, the parent company of Sportskeeda, increasing its total ownership to 91%.{{cite web |date=18 September 2024 |title=Nazara Technologies raises stake in Sportskeeda parent to over 90% with ₹145.5 crore deal |website=CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/nazara-technologies-buys-additional-19-4-stake-in-absolute-sports-for-rs-145-5-crore-19478681.htm |access-date=3 April 2025}} In 2025, Nazara Technologies acquired Curve Games, the parent company of Sportskeeda, 100% for ₹247 crore, increasing its total ownership to 100%.{{cite web |date=21 May 2025 |title=Nazara Tech bets on $100 billion console market with Curve Games acquisition |website=CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/companies/nazara-tech-bets-on-dollar-100-billion-console-market-with-curve-games-acquisition-19607728.htm |access-date=3 April 2025 }} == Games == * ''[[World Cricket Championship (mobile game series)|World Cricket Championship]]'' * ''Kiddopia'' * ''[[Animal Jam Classic]]'' * ''Motu Patlu Run'' == extract: Nazara Technologies is an Indian video game development company that has business interests in mobile games, esports, and sports media. Founded in 1999, it is based in Mumbai, India, and through the years acquired several companies turned into subsidiaries, including WildWorks, Curve Games, and Sportskeeda.
